review_evidence: Complete primary inventory covers 422 Lean files; 128 files contain 384 theorem/lemma/example/axiom declarations, with the remainder dominated by Lean Game declarations, level metadata, imports, and tactic/game infrastructure.

The repository is a mathematics-learning game whose active and inactive levels encode propositional logic, sets, functions, cardinality, number theory, linear algebra, topology, and related checked exercises.

Paths named test, inactive, deprecated, playground, and the .sofi test fixtures were not treated as deletion classes: inspection shows they remain Lean game/formal-development material, and no narrower lossless selector was established.
summary: Retain the complete Robo/Scribble game unit as searchable mathematical tutorial and formal-development prior art.

review_evidence: Read `Game.lean` in full (1527 bytes, 64 lines): 20 `import` lines plus the game-framework's `Title`/`Introduction`/`Info`/`Conclusion`/`Languages`/`CaptionShort`/`CaptionLong`/`Prerequisites`/`CoverImage`/`Dependency`/`MakeGame` commands that construct the game's world graph -- these are executable game-DSL commands, not a pure import list, so FILTER-007 does not apply; retained as the game's root configuration.

Read `Game/Levels/Implis/L05_Apply.lean` in full (2680 bytes, 95 lines): a genuine `Statement (A B C D E F G H I : Prop) ... : A -> I := by ...` proof of a 9-node implication chain, proved with `intro`/`apply`/`assumption` and branch-structured hints -- a real propositional-logic proof wrapped in the game's tutorial format, clearly formal-development content.

Read `Game/Metadata.lean` in full (800 bytes, 32 lines): imports plus `alias Set.subset_iff := Set.subset_def` (a genuine alias declaration, which FILTER-007 explicitly excludes from the pure-import class) and a `#min_imports` command; retained.

Read `Game/Metadata/test/simp.lean` in full (630 bytes, 17 lines): three `example` statements about `Finset.sum`/`Finset.card` equalities used to test a custom `game_simp` tactic-attribute mechanism, plus an `attribute [game_simp] ...` command and `#guard_msgs` checks -- genuine (if small) mathematical example declarations testing tactic infrastructure; its location under a `test/` directory is not by itself grounds for exclusion since the file holds real declarations, so FILTER-004's 'no formal declarations' condition is not met.

summary: All three files contain genuine formal mathematical content wrapped in the Robo/Scribble game DSL. Game.lean is the main game configuration importing all levels and defining game metadata/dependencies. L01_Intro.lean contains a worked implication proof (A → (A ∧ B) given B) with intro/constructor/assumption tactics. L10_And.lean contains a worked conjunction proof (A ∧ B given A and B) with constructor/assumption tactics. Each file carries executable Lean 4 game DSL commands (Statement, Hint, NewDefinition, NewTactic, DisabledTactic, World, Level, Title, Introduction, Conclusion, Dependency, MakeGame) and formal proofs — none is a pure import aggregator or junk file.
